context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring regulatory compliance, interoperability, and low-bandwidth availability.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (External Actors)
- Telehealth Platform (EU) (`europe-west3`) and Telehealth Platform (US) (`us-central1`) (Regional Systems)
- Global Media Relay Network (External WebRTC Infrastructure)
- National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks (External Systems)
- Identity & Consent Providers (Regional External IDPs)
- AI Model Registry & Inference Provider (External ML Service)
- API Gateway / BFF (Cloud Run / Cloud Load Balancing)
- Consultation Service & AI Proxy & Audit Service (GKE Microservices)
- Consent & Identity Service & E-Prescription Integration Service (Cloud Run Containers)
- Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage (Regional Persistence)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to Global Media Relay Network via WebRTC/UDP/TCP over TLS (Video consultations)
- Patients & Clinicians to API Gateway / BFF via HTTPS/WebSockets (Signaling and app interactions)
- API Gateway to Regional Microservices via internal gRPC over mTLS
- E-Prescription Integration Service to National Gateways/Pharmacy Networks via HTTPS/REST (HL7 FHIR in US)
- AI Proxy Service to AI Model Registry via gRPC/HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Selected for robust regional isolation (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`).
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) & Cloud Run: Used for container orchestration and scalable microservices.
- WebRTC: Enables low-bandwidth video down to 300 kbit/s via edge relays.
- Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) & Cloud Storage: Provides regional persistence with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK).
- Google Cloud Pub/Sub: Powers asynchronous audit logging for AI traceability.

## Rationale
Splitting the system into two distinct regional platforms guarantees compliance with GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Delegating media streaming to edge relays and utilizing gRPC over mTLS ensures high availability in degraded network conditions and secure, low-latency internal communication.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring high availability for unstable connections.

## Key Elements
* Web & Mobile Clients (React / React Native)
* API Gateway & Routing (Kong / GCP API Gateway)
* Core Telehealth Service (Java / Spring Boot)
* WebRTC Media Broker (Node.js / Mediasoup)
* AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
* FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service (Python / Java)
* Consent & Audit Logging Service (Go)
* Messaging (Cloud Pub/Sub)
* Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage)

## Relationships
* Web & Mobile Clients -> API Gateway (TLS 1.3 over HTTPS, WSS)
* API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Service & AI Symptom Checker (gRPC via internal VPC Service Controls)
* Core Telehealth Service -> WebRTC Media Broker (gRPC, WebSockets/UDP)
* AI Symptom Checker -> Cloud Pub/Sub (gRPC)
* FHIR Integration Service -> National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Networks (HTTPS with mTLS)
* Consent & Audit Logging Service -> Cloud Storage (Encrypted via CMEK)

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Region-isolated cloud infrastructure ensuring strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance.
* Java/Spring Boot & Python/FastAPI: Robust backend runtimes for telehealth logic and AI inference.
* Node.js / Mediasoup: SFU-based WebRTC routing supporting degraded modes below 300 kbit/s.
* Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage: Region-isolated transactional stores and cryptographically bound audit logs.
* VPC Service Controls & Cloud KMS: Perimeter security and Customer-Managed Encryption Keys enforcing data residency.

## Rationale
The architecture strictly isolates EU and US health data within designated GCP regions using VPC Service Controls and CMEK to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Furthermore, Mediasoup-based WebRTC streaming and decoupled asynchronous logging ensure rural availability and traceable AI medical outputs.

Web & Mobile Clients.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients using GCP regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`. It ensures strict data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and uninterrupted availability for rural users.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Web & Mobile Clients Container (React, React Native, TypeScript)
- 11 Client Components: Patient Portal App, Clinician Workspace App, WebRTC Media Client Module, Local State & Storage Manager, AI Symptom Checker UI Module, E-Prescription & FHIR Viewer, Consent & Privacy Manager, Telemetry & Audit Logger, Adaptive Bitrate Controller, Regional Endpoint Router, Secure Token & Session Manager
- API Gateway & Routing Container (Kong / GCP API Gateway)
- Core Telehealth Service Container (Java / Spring Boot)
- WebRTC Media Broker Container (Node.js / Mediasoup)
- AI Symptom Checker Service Container (Python / FastAPI)
- FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service Container (Python / Java)
- Consent & Audit Logging Service Container (Go)
- Messaging and Databases (Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web & Mobile Clients: Accesses telehealth features [HTTPS, WSS]
- Web & Mobile Clients -> Regional Endpoint Router: Pins geographic context [In-memory routing]
- Regional Endpoint Router -> API Gateway & Routing: Transmits regional requests [TLS 1.3 over HTTPS]
- WebRTC Media Client Module -> WebRTC Media Broker: Streams video [UDP/DTLS via ICE/STUN/TURN]
- Consent & Privacy Manager, Telemetry & Audit Logger -> API Gateway: Transmits consent and audit payloads [TLS 1.3 over HTTPS]
- API Gateway & Routing -> Core Telehealth, AI Symptom Checker, and Integration Services: Routes authenticated traffic [gRPC / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React & React Native: Maximizes code sharing across web, iOS, and Android clients.
- IndexedDB & SQLite: Provides local offline caching to handle unstable rural connections (R-06).
- WebRTC & Mediasoup: Enables peer-to-peer and SFU video consultations.
- TypeScript: Ensures type safety across client modules and the Regional Endpoint Router.
- OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Secures session management and token refreshes.

## Rationale
This architecture uses client-side regional routing and offline storage to satisfy GDPR/HIPAA data residency and rural availability constraints. Decoupling WebRTC media streaming and local state management ensures low-bandwidth resilience and high-quality video consultations.

API Gateway & Routing.analysis:
## Overview
[A secure cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US.]
[Enforces strict regional data residency and regulatory compliance using a distributed GCP cloud architecture.]

## Key Elements
* **Web & Mobile Clients**: React / React Native user interface for patients and clinicians.
* **API Gateway & Routing**: Kong Enterprise container managing ingress, WAF, geo-routing, and security.
* **Core Telehealth Service**: Java / Spring Boot container handling consultations and appointments.
* **WebRTC Media Broker**: Node.js / Mediasoup container managing real-time video streams.
* **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Python / FastAPI container delivering urgency recommendations.
* **FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service**: Python / Java container handling regional prescription standards.
* **Consent & Audit Logging Service**: Go container managing user consents and traceability logs.
* **Messaging & Storage**: Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, and Cloud Storage.

## Relationships
* **Web & Mobile Clients** -> **API Gateway & Routing**: Sends client requests, WSS signaling, and HTTPS traffic [TLS 1.3 over HTTPS, WSS].
* **API Gateway & Routing** -> **Core Telehealth Service**: Routes telehealth requests via VPC Service Controls [gRPC over mTLS].
* **API Gateway & Routing** -> **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Routes AI inference requests via VPC Service Controls [gRPC over mTLS].
* **API Gateway & Routing** -> **WebRTC Media Broker**: Relays real-time signaling [gRPC / TCP].
* **FHIR & Prescription Protocol Router** -> **FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service**: Forwards regional health data payloads [gRPC over VPC SC].

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Provider**: GCP (regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`) for regional data isolation.
* **API Gateway**: Kong Enterprise with WAF, geo-routing, and mTLS termination plugins.
* **Backend Services**: Java / Spring Boot (Core Telehealth), Python / FastAPI (AI & FHIR integration), Go (Consent & Audit).
* **Real-Time Communication**: Node.js / Mediasoup for WebRTC media bridging.
* **Data & Messaging**: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, and Cloud Pub/Sub.

## Rationale
[The multi-region GCP architecture guarantees strict compliance with EU GDPR and US HIPAA mandates by physically separating health data into `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.]
[Kong Enterprise edge routing, gRPC over mTLS, and internal VPC Service Controls ensure secure, low-latency, and traceable cross-border telemedicine operations.]

- Data Residency Guard -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Enforces region-locked connection strings (`europe-west3` / `us-central1`) [JDBC/TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Core Telehealth Service implementation using modular monolith boundaries, Spring Application Events, and Spring Security aspects for consent enforcement
- GCP (regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`): Target cloud provider for strict data residency and VPC Service Controls
- gRPC / Protobuf: Primary protocol for high-performance internal microservice and container communication
- Cloud Pub/Sub: Asynchronous messaging for event-driven workflows and audit logging
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Region-isolated relational storage utilizing thread-local regional context

## Rationale
This architecture uses GCP VPC Service Controls, strict data residency guards, and regional routing to satisfy rigorous GDPR and HIPAA compliance mandates. Additionally, the inclusion of a dedicated Degraded Mode Adaptor and audit event streaming ensures high availability in rural areas and complete traceability for medical AI outputs.

WebRTC Media Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It guarantees strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability for low-bandwidth users.

## Key Elements
- Web & Mobile Clients (React / React Native)
- Signaling & Room Manager (Node.js/TypeScript)
- SFU Core Router (Mediasoup C++ worker wrapper)
- Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Controller (Node.js)
- NAT Traversal Agents (GCP STUN/TURN integration)
- Media Region Router
- Media Session Logger
- Media Encryption Enforcer
- STUN/TURN Health & Metrics Exporter
- Consent & Audit Logging Service (Go)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Clients -> Signaling & Room Manager: WebSocket [WSS]
- Web & Mobile Clients -> SFU Core Router: WebRTC [ICE/DTLS/SRTP over UDP/TCP]
- SFU Core Router <-> Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Controller: Asynchronous Worker IPC
- Media Session Logger -> Consent & Audit Logging Service: Regional Telemetry [gRPC]
- STUN/TURN Health & Metrics Exporter -> Core Telehealth Service: Health Check [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Cloud infrastructure ensuring strict data residency per region
- Node.js & Mediasoup: Real-time media streaming and Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) capabilities
- DTLS-SRTP with AES-GCM: Native secure transport configuration for encrypted media streams
- WebSockets & WebRTC: Low-latency client-server signaling and peer-to-peer media transport

## Rationale
The component architecture isolates media handling into regional GCP nodes to satisfy strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Using Mediasoup with an adaptive bitrate controller ensures uninterrupted video consultations for rural patients on unstable connections below 300 kbit/s.

FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Servic.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. Built on GCP to ensure strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for rural connectivity.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (Users)
* Web & Mobile Clients (React / React Native)
* API Gateway & Routing (Kong / GCP API Gateway)
* Core Telehealth Service (Java / Spring Boot)
* WebRTC Media Broker (Node.js / Mediasoup)
* AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
* FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service (Python / Java)
* Consent & Audit Logging Service (Go)
* Messaging (Cloud Pub/Sub)
* Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage)
* National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) and US Pharmacy Networks

## Relationships
* Web & Mobile Clients -> API Gateway & Routing: HTTPS / WSS
* API Gateway & Routing -> Core Telehealth Service: gRPC / REST
* Core Telehealth Service -> WebRTC Media Broker: WebRTC / gRPC
* Core Telehealth Service -> AI Symptom Checker Service: gRPC / REST
* Core Telehealth Service -> FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service: gRPC / REST
* FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service -> National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Networks: HTTPS with mTLS
* All Services -> Consent & Audit Logging Service: gRPC over TLS

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce data residency
* Backend Services: Java (Spring Boot) and Python (FastAPI) for core logic and AI
* Integration: Java (HAPI FHIR) for US Core profiles and national eHDSI/OpenNCP standards
* Messaging & Resilience: Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous retry queues during network partitions
* Communication: gRPC for internal service-to-service communication; HTTPS with mTLS for external integrations

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces regional isolation between EU and US data processing to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Asynchronous queuing via Cloud Pub/Sub guarantees prescription delivery and telehealth availability for patients with unstable rural internet connections.

Consent & Audit Logging Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Consent & Audit Logging Service manages patient data consent and immutable audit trails for a cross-border telehealth platform operating in the EU and US. Its core purpose is to enforce strict regional data residency and regulatory traceability for GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR compliance.]

## Key Elements
* Consent API Handler Component (Go, `grpc-go`, `net/http`)
* Consent Manager Component (Go, Open Policy Agent)
* Audit Logger Component (Go, Crypto-Shredding & Hashing Sub-component)
* Compliance Export Component (Go)
* Storage Abstraction Layer (Go, CMEK Key Management Interface)
* Cloud Pub/Sub
* Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (europe-west3, us-central1)
* Cloud Storage (WORM configuration)
* GCP KMS

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Consent API Handler: gRPC over HTTP/2
* Core Telehealth Service & AI Symptom Checker Service -> Consent Manager: gRPC synchronous checks
* Cloud Pub/Sub -> Audit Logger: AMQP/PubSub protocol
* Consent API Handler -> Consent Manager & Audit Logger: In-process Go function calls / channels
* Audit Logger -> Cloud Storage (WORM): HTTPS/Storage API
* Consent Manager -> Regional Cloud SQL Databases: PostgreSQL wire protocol via TLS 1.3
* Storage Abstraction Layer -> GCP KMS: gRPC/Cloud KMS API via TLS 1.3
* Compliance Export Component -> Storage Abstraction Layer: Internal Go interface calls

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for high-performance backend components and concurrency support.
* Open Policy Agent (OPA): Embedded for rapid, stateless GDPR and HIPAA access rule evaluations.
* Cloud SQL & Cloud Storage: Provides regional persistence with WORM capabilities.
* GCP KMS: Enforces regional Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK).

## Rationale
[This architecture uses regional service boundaries, cryptographic tamper-evidence, and policy-driven enforcement to satisfy strict EU/US data residency mandates. The component design ensures full compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR traceability requirements without sacrificing system availability.]

Messaging.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilient messaging for unstable connections.

## Key Elements
- EU Pub/Sub Topic Partition (`europe-west3`)
- US Pub/Sub Topic Partition (`us-central1`)
- Event Schema Registry
- Client Ingress Relay
- Regional Message Forwarders
- Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) & Retry Handler Component
- DLQ Monitoring & Alerting Component

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Clients -> Client Ingress Relay via WebSocket/MQTT [WSS]
- Client Ingress Relay -> Regional Pub/Sub Topics via GCP Pub/Sub [gRPC]
- Core Telehealth & AI Services -> Event Schema Registry via [HTTPS/gRPC]
- Regional Pub/Sub Topics -> Regional Message Forwarders via [gRPC]
- Regional Pub/Sub Topics -> DLQ & Monitoring via [gRPC/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- GCP Pub/Sub: Asynchronous messaging backbone with regional partitioning for data residency.
- Apache Avro / JSON Schema: Payload validation enforced via Event Schema Registry.
- WebSocket / MQTT: Edge connectivity protocol for handling rural, low-bandwidth clients.
- Java / Go: Implementation languages for regional message forwarders and workers.
- Cloud Monitoring / Cloud Functions: Automated alerting for DLQ and poisoned messages.

## Rationale
Regional topic isolation and strict schema validation guarantee compliance with GDPR and HIPAA data residency and audit requirements. Edge relay buffering and dead-letter monitoring ensure continuous availability and resilience over unstable rural internet connections.

Databases.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Global Media Relay Network, National E-Prescription Gateways (EU), US Pharmacy Networks, Identity & Consent Providers, AI Model Registry & Inference Provider (External Systems)
- Web & Mobile Clients (React / React Native)
- API Gateway & Routing (Kong / GCP API Gateway)
- Core Telehealth Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- WebRTC Media Broker (Node.js / Mediasoup)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service (Python / Java)
- Consent & Audit Logging Service (Go)
- Messaging (Cloud Pub/Sub)
- Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Regional Memorystore for Redis)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Clients -> API Gateway & Routing: HTTPS / WSS over TLS 1.3
- API Gateway & Routing -> Core Telehealth Service: gRPC / REST over TLS 1.3
- Core Telehealth Service -> WebRTC Media Broker: WebRTC / DTLS over UDP/TCP
- AI Symptom Checker Service -> AI Model Registry & Inference Provider: HTTPS over TLS 1.3
- FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service -> National E-Prescription Gateways / US Pharmacy Networks: HL7 FHIR / National APIs over TLS 1.3
- Consent & Audit Logging Service -> Databases: Stores audit logs and consent records encrypted via CMEK (Cloud Storage / Cloud SQL)

## Technology Stack
- GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Cloud provider and isolated regional hosting ensuring data residency.
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Regional transactional databases with Row-Level Security (RLS) for patient data and consent enforcement.
- Cloud Storage: Regional WORM buckets with CMEK for immutable AI traceability logging.
- Regional Memorystore for Redis: Fast patient-to-region mapping caches.
- React / React Native: Cross-platform web and mobile client interfaces.
- Java (Spring Boot) & Python (FastAPI): Robust backend services for telehealth logic and AI processing.
- WebRTC (Mediasoup): Real-time video communication supporting degraded connection modes.

## Rationale
This architecture strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates by isolating all operational data and backups within regional GCP boundaries. Furthermore, it guarantees compliance, auditability, and interoperability through regional database partitioning, cryptographic logging, and adherence to local healthcare standards.
